title: group_multicast_from_id leaks UnicodeEncodeError
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py group_multicast_from_id() documents AddrError for bad group ids and already rejects non-str and empty. The 16-bit group field is SHA-256(UTF-8(id))[0:2].

A Python str with unpaired surrogates is type str and non-empty, so it passes the guard, then:

  group_id.encode('utf-8')  # UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed

Verified: group_multicast_from_id('\\ud800') raises UnicodeEncodeError, not AddrError. Every other public helper in this file maps stdlib value errors to AddrError (to_ipv6, make_link_local zone parse, native_address_from_pubkey).

## Why it matters

Callers (CoAP /groups) catch AddrError. A lone surrogate in a group name escapes that handler and becomes a 5.00 instead of 4.00.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:254-268 group_multicast_from_id
python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py:121-123 mcast_from_id
design: Keep SHA-256(UTF-8(id)) as specified. Catch UnicodeEncodeError from group_id.encode('utf-8') and raise AddrError from it, same as to_ipv6 wrapping ValueError. Do not NFC-normalize unless the spec adds that; this issue is only the exception type at the public boundary. Empty/non-str already raise AddrError.
acceptance_criteria: group_multicast_from_id('\ud800') raises AddrError (not UnicodeEncodeError). group_multicast_from_id('team-alpha') still matches the pinned SHA-256 high-16 oracle 0x29c4. Existing empty/non-str tests still raise AddrError.
